name: Chouka
why_it_matters: The Assamese restaurant Lonely Planet calls 'hard-pressed to find better Assamese cooking anywhere'. Specialist chef cooks bamboo shoots, banana flowers, elephant apple, mustard greens, sesame-seed sauces, fish in tenga, and items steamed in banana leaves. 4.3 across 1,379 Google reviews, 4.7 on Tripadvisor. Now expanding to Guwahati. The default Jorhat lunch.
insider_tip: Pork thali is the order — the dish that made Chouka's reputation. The bamboo shoots are sourced fresh, not preserved (this matters in flavour). Lunch is busier than dinner; aim for 12:30pm sharp or post-2:30pm.

name: Meridian Restaurant
why_it_matters: Tripadvisor #2 of 84 Jorhat restaurants (4.5). The Assamese thali is customisable — 11-13 dishes daily depending on what's at market, swappable for local fish, duck, chicken or mutton. 'Ari mas' (the giant catfish from the Brahmaputra) is the order to ask about when in season. Closed Sundays.
insider_tip: Closed Sunday — verify before showing up. The thali is the value play; à-la-carte loses to the thali on price-per-dish ratio. Caters parties up to 100, so weekday lunch slots fill with office groups around 1pm.
